Maledon''' ({{IPA|fr|teo malɛdɔ̃|lang}};{{cite web|title=Focus on: Theo Maledon, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lDJagrDebiA|publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball]]|time=00:26|date=20 February 2020|access-date=3 April 2022}} born 12 June 2001) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Born in [[Rouen]], Maledon played youth basketball for French sports institute [[INSEP]] before joining the youth ranks of [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] at age 16. One year later, at the senior level, he became the youngest [[LNB All-Star Game|LNB All-Star]] in history and won the [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player]] award. He helped ASVEL win Pro A and [[French Basketball Cup|French Cup]] titles, while being named [[French Basketball Cup Final MVP|French Cup Final Most Valuable Player]] (MVP). At the youth international level, Maledon won a gold medal with [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]] and a silver medal at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]]. He has also played for the [[France national basketball team|senior national team]]. ==Early life and career== Maledon was born on 12 June 2001 in [[Rouen]] in Normandy, France.{{cite web |title=Talents du Parisien. Basket : Théo Maledon comme une évidence |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/sports/ile-de-france/talents-du-parisien-basket-theo-maledon-comme-une-evidence-15-06-2017-7052694.php |website=[[Le Parisien]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |language=fr |date=15 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328231333/http://www.leparisien.fr/sports/ile-de-france/talents-du-parisien-basket-theo-maledon-comme-une-evidence-15-06-2017-7052694.php |archive-date=28 March 2019 |url-status=live }} He is of Guadeloupean descent.{{Cite web|url=https://www.guadeloupe.franceantilles.fr/actualite/sports/basket-ball/le-basketteur-theo-maledon-candidat-a-la-draft-nba-686608.php|title=Le basketteur Théo Maledon candidat à la draft NBA|date=28 June 2023|website=guadeloupe.franceantilles.fr}} At age three, Maledon began playing basketball with his local club [[Le Mesnil-Esnard|Mesnil-Esnard]] in [[Seine-Maritime]].{{cite web |last=Callier |first=Sylvie |title=Le basketteur rouennais Théo Maledon part pour l'ASVEL (Villeurbanne) |url=https://france3-regions.francetvinfo.fr/normandie/seine-maritime/rouen/basketteur-rouennais-theo-maledon-part-asvel-villeurbanne-1316471.html |publisher=[[France 3 Normandie]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |language=fr |date=25 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328231204/https://france3-regions.francetvinfo.fr/normandie/seine-maritime/rouen/basketteur-rouennais-theo-maledon-part-asvel-villeurbanne-1316471.html |archive-date=28 March 2019 |url-status=live }} After reaching the under-11 age group, he moved to [[Rouen Métropole Basket|SPO Rouen]], the most prominent club in his area. In 2015, at age 14, Maledon joined the National Institute of Sport, Expertise, and Performance ([[INSEP]]), a sports institute in [[Paris]], on a scholarship.{{cite web |title=Théo Maledon à l'Asvel ===ASVEL (2017–2020)=== ====2017–18 season==== On 16 June 2017, Maledon joined the junior team of [[LNB Pro A]] club [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] that played in the {{ill|lt=LNB Espoirs|Championnat de France de basket-ball Espoirs|fr}}, the French U21 league. In his season debut on 24 September 2017, he recorded 10 points and five assists in a 71–61 win over Espoirs [[Limoges CSP|Limoges]].{{cite web |title=Sep 24, 2017 – Espoirs Limoges 61, Espoirs Lyon 71 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-09-24/Espoirs-Limoges-at-Espoirs-Lyon/290296 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=24 September 2017}} Maledon made his Pro A debut for the senior team on 30 September at age 16, playing one minute versus [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]].{{cite web |title=Sep 30, 2017 – Cholet Basket 59, ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne 77 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-09-30/Cholet-Basket-at-ASVEL-Lyon-Villeurbanne/285178 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=30 September 2017}} He became the second youngest debutant in club history.{{cite web |title=Théo Maledon (ASVEL), un ado parmi les hommes |url=https://www.lnb.fr/fr/article/theo-maledon-asvel-un-ado-parmi-les-hommes-12071.html |publisher=[[Ligue nationale de basket]] |access-date=27 December 2018 |language=fr |date=14 November 2017}} On 17 October, he made his first appearance in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] against [[ratiopharm Ulm]].{{cite web |title=Oct 17, 2017 – Ratiopharm Ulm 77, ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne 108 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-10-17/Ratiopharm-Ulm-at-ASVEL-Lyon-Villeurbanne/269804 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=17 October 2017}} In January 2018, Maledon played for ASVEL's under-18 team at the [[2017–18 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|ANGT]] in [[L'Hospitalet de Llobregat|L'Hospitalet]]. He recorded 35 points and 11 assists on 7 January to help defeat the junior team of [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]] in his final game in the tournament.{{cite web |title=Great performance in the Euroleague's Adidas Next Generation Tournament |url=https://cbgrancanaria.net/en/news/great-performance-in-the-euroleagues-adidas-next-generation-tournament/ |publisher=[[CB Gran Canaria]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=8 January 2018 |archive-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131035208/https://cbgrancanaria.net/en/news/great-performance-in-the-euroleagues-adidas-next-generation-tournament/ |url-status=dead }} On 12 May 2018, Maledon scored 26 points against Espoirs [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]], his season-high in the LNB Espoirs.{{cite web |title=May 12, 2018 – Espoirs Monaco 90, Espoirs Lyon 81 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-05-12/Espoirs-Monaco-at-Espoirs-Lyon/291802 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=12 May 2018}} Through 33 Espoirs games, he averaged 15.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game. During summer 2018, he graduated high school one year in advance with major in science.{{Cite web|url=https://www.leparisien.fr/sports/equipe-de-france-de-basket-theo-maledon-un-meneur-a-suivre-21-02-2019-8016987.php|title=Equipe de France de basket : Théo Maledon, un meneur à suivre|date=21 February 2019}} ====2018–19 season==== [[File:Theo Maledon Benoit Mangin (cropped).jpg|thumb|Maledon (left) defends [[ESSM Le Portel|Le Portel]]'s Benoît Mangin in December 2018.]] On 13 August 2018, Maledon signed his first professional contract, agreeing to remain with ASVEL for three years.{{cite web |title=ASVEL signs young Maledon for 3 years |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8xtiggmw587nkulp/asvel-signs-young-maledon-for-3-years |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball]] |access-date=26 December 2018 |date=13 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181223235152/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8xtiggmw587nkulp/asvel-signs-young-maledon-for-3-years |archive-date=23 December 2018 |url-status=dead }} In the [[2018–19 EuroLeague|2018–19 season]], he assumed a greater role for the senior team and frequently made its starting lineup. |title=Panathinaikos overpowers ASVEL |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1009516/panathinaikos-overpowers-asvel/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=15 February 2020 |date=24 January 2020 February, Maledon matched his career high in scoring with 20 points in an 88–59 victory over [[Metropolitans 92]] at the [[LNB Pro A Leaders Cup]] semifinals.{{cite news |last=Borghesan |first=Ennio |url-status=live }} On 5 April, while the basketball season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]]. Maledon finished the season averaging 7.3 points, 2.7 assists, and 1.9 rebounds in 17.3 minutes per game, through 46 combined appearances in the EuroLeague, Pro A and Leaders Cup. ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2022)=== Maledon was selected with the 34th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the 2020 NBA draft.{{cite web |last=Noriega |first=Edith |title=NBA draft 2020: Five things to know about international prospect Theo Maledon |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2020/11/18/theo-maledon-french-teen-nba-draft-76-ers-second-round/6340209002/ |website=USA Today |access-date=8 December 2020 |date=18 November 2020}} On 8 December 2020, Maledon's draft rights were traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]],{{cite web |title=Thunder Acquires Al Horford, the Draft Rights to Théo Maledon and Vasilije Micić, and 2025 First-Round Draft Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-201208 |website=NBA.com |access-date=8 December 2020 |date=8 December December 2020}} On 30 September 2022 Maledon was traded, along with [[Derrick Favors]], [[Ty Jerome]], [[Maurice Harkless]], and a future second-round pick, to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[David Nwaba]], [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]], [[Trey Burke]], and [[Marquese Chriss]].{{cite web |last=Peery |first=Hannah |title=Rockets Complete Trade with Oklahoma City |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-oklahoma-city |website=NBA.com |date=September 30, 2022 |access-date=October 1, 2022}} On 11 October he was waived.{{Cite web |language=en}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2022–2023)=== On 15 October 2022, Maledon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Theo Maledon To Two-Way with the Hornets on another two-way contract,{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Re-Sign Théo Maledon|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-re-sign-theo-maledon|website=NBA.com|date=29 Maledon|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-theo-maledon|website=NBA.com|date=14 December 2023|access-date=14 December 2023}} ===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)=== On 17 December 2023, Maledon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite tweet|author=Phoenix Suns|title=Welcome to The Valley, Théo! 🏜️|number=1736521680036741555|user=Suns|date=17 December 2023|access-date=17 with the team until 8 February 2024, playing in only a minute and 14 seconds left of the Suns' 129–115 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz vs Phoenix Suns - Box [[Valentine's Day]] during nearly 10 minutes of playing time in a 116–100 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons at Phoenix Suns Box Score, February 14, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202402140PHO.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=5 March 2024}} Maledon was waived on 4 March 2024 after playing in four games 2024}} However, he never played for them. ===Return to ASVEL (2024–2025)=== On 14 August 2024, Maledon returned to [[ASVEL Basket|LDLC ASVEL]].{{cite web|title=Théo Maledon est de scoring 23 points, 2 rebounds and 7 assists in a game against Real Madrid. Through seven games, he averaged 8.4 points, four rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Theo Maledon's profile |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/131498/pid2//sid/12295/tid/282/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U16_European_Championship_Division_A/index.html |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=27 December
